details: is a Canadian technology company conducting research in artificial intelligence and language understanding. Founded in 2011, the company was acquired by Microsoft in 2017. In late March 2016, the company demonstrated a machine reading system capable of answering arbitrary questions about J.K Rowling’s Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone. Maluuba's natural language understanding technology is used by several consumer electronic brands for over 50 million devices.

explainer.lead: Maluuba was a Canadian artificial-intelligence company focused on helping computers understand language. Its work connected machine-reading research with technology used in consumer electronics before Microsoft acquired it in 2017.

tiers.eli5: Maluuba was a Canadian company that taught computers to understand language. Imagine reading a story and then asking a computer questions about what happened; that is the kind of task its machine-reading system demonstrated. It later became part of Microsoft.
tiers.practitioner: For an engineer, Maluuba illustrates natural-language understanding research moving into consumer electronics rather than a standalone algorithm or software library. Its 2016 demonstration framed machine reading as answering arbitrary questions about a book; no implementation stack or model architecture is specified.
